questionText:
Consider the following three relations in a relational database.

$Employee(\underline{eId}, Name), Brand(\underline{bId}, bName), Own(\underline{eId},\underline{bId})$

Which of the following relational algebra expressions return the set of $eIds$ who own all the brands?
explanation:
To find all $eIds$ who own all the brands, we can use either the division operator or the universal quantification using set difference (double negation).

1. Using Division Operator (Option A):
The division operator $R / S$ finds tuples in $R$ that are associated with all tuples in $S$.
Here, $\Pi_{eId, bId}(Own) / \Pi_{bId}(Brand)$ returns the $eIds$ that are paired with every $bId$ in $Brand$. Outer projection $\Pi_{eId}$ is redundant but mathematically correct.
Thus, Option A is correct.

2. Using Cartesian Product & Set Difference (Option B):
• $\Pi_{eId}(Own) \times \Pi_{bId}(Brand)$: Represents all possible $(eId, bId)$ pairs for employees who own at least one brand.
• $(\Pi_{eId}(Own) \times \Pi_{bId}(Brand)) - \Pi_{eId,bId}(Own)$: Gives $(eId, bId)$ pairs representing brands that an employee does not own.
• $\Pi_{eId}(\dots)$: Gives the set of $eIds$ who fail to own at least one brand.
• $\Pi_{eId}(Own) - \dots$: Subtracting these from all employee $eIds$ yields the $eIds$ who own all brands.
Thus, Option B is correct.
